discrepancies.topic: First templated index.html ignores the name argument

a.value: 'try adding ?name=[Your Name] to the base URL' after app.py passes name=request.args.get("name", "world")

b.value: With the index.html shown just before (body 'hello, world', no {{ name }}), GET /?name=David still renders 'hello, world'; the placeholder appears only in the src9 hello versions that use {{ name }}

discrepancies.note: w09-n03 shows the official files verbatim and adds an authored one-line change (hello, {{ name }}) labelled تألیفی so the experiment does what the notes promise.

a.value: 'app.py contains code the tells Flask how to run your web application'

b.value: intended: 'code that tells Flask'

discrepancies.note: Typo only.

discrepancies.topic: 'Hello,' vs 'hello,' and when the default applies

a.value: 'when someone types in no name into the form, Hello, is displayed without a name'

b.value: greet.html prints lowercase 'hello,'. A submitted empty field gives '' (request.form.get("name", "world") falls back only when the key is missing): POST name='' -> 'hello,'; POST without the field -> 'hello, world'

discrepancies.note: w09-n07 explains both: capitalisation in the notes' prose only, and why the fix moves the default into {% if name %} (an empty string is falsy).

a.value: 'Notice that name=request.form.get("name")) is changed.'

b.value: the code itself has render_template("greet.html", name=request.form.get("name")) with balanced parentheses

discrepancies.note: Typo in the prose only.

a.value: shows1 app.py: db.execute(... LIKE ?, "%" + request.args.get("q") + "%")

b.value: GET /search (no q) raises TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "NoneType") to str at line 16 -> HTTP 500. The next version (shows2) adds 'if q: ... else: shows = []' and returns an empty result

discrepancies.note: w09-n14 keeps shows1 verbatim and points to the shows2 guard as the fix; a spot_bug challenge uses an authored variant.

discrepancies.topic: JSON example escapes in the wrong order and only once

a.value: let title = shows[i].title.replace('<', '<').replace('&', '&');

b.value: node 20: '<b>' becomes '&lt;b>' (displayed as the literal text <b>), and 'a<b<c' becomes 'a&lt;b<c': a string pattern replaces only the first match, and & must be escaped before <

discrepancies.note: w09-n15 keeps the code verbatim; an authored callout shows the safer habit (escape & first with replaceAll, or set textContent) — verified in node and jsdom.

a.value: fetch('/search?q=' + input.value)

b.value: Flask receives q='Tom ' for the raw URL /search?q=Tom & Jerry, but 'Tom & Jerry' when the value is encoded (encodeURIComponent gives Tom%20%26%20Jerry)

discrepancies.note: Authored callout in w09-n14 recommends encodeURIComponent (inference + box run).

a.value: 'You can read more in the AJAX documentation' -> https://api.jquery.com/category/ajax/

b.value: the lecture code uses the built-in fetch with async/await, not jQuery

discrepancies.note: Persian note keeps the official link and adds MDN's fetch page as the matching reference.

discrepancies.topic: search input type changes between versions

a.value: shows1/shows2 index.html: <input ... type="search">

b.value: shows3 index.html: <input ... type="text">

discrepancies.note: Both work; type=search only adds a clear button in some browsers (inference).

a.value: SELECT * FROM shows WHERE title LIKE ? LIMIT 50

b.value: without ORDER BY the set of 50 rows returned is not defined by SQL (SQLite usually returns rowid order)

discrepancies.note: Week 7 knowledge; mentioned in w09-n14 as a tip (inference, labelled).

discrepancies.topic: 'looks to see if session["name"] exists' vs the template

a.value: 'Notice that this file looks to see if session["name"] exists'

b.value: login index.html tests {% if name %}; app.py passes name=session.get("name")

discrepancies.note: The template sees the value through the name variable; the check on the session happens in app.py. w09-n12 states this.

a.value: store: session["cart"].append(book_id) then SELECT * FROM books WHERE id IN (?) with session["cart"]

b.value: With Flask-Session (filesystem) the appended id persists to the next request; with an empty cart cs50 9.5.0 runs the query and returns no rows (box run)

discrepancies.note: Recorded as verified behaviour; no change.
